ADDICTION MEDICINE NOTE   Date: 2026-04-20
53M, emergency room encounter with follow-up in the outpatient program.

S:
Patient was seen in the emergency room and is reviewed here for continuity of his outpatient program care. He reports that cravings have been strong over the past two weeks, worse in the evenings and after stressful shifts. He attends group twice weekly and individual counseling on Thursdays, though he missed two sessions recently. He works as a line cook. He could not complete 9 of his scheduled shifts last month because of symptoms. No shortness of breath. Sleep is poor, averaging about 5 hours. Appetite is fair. Lives alone; a brother checks in regularly. Taking medications as prescribed.

O:
BP 128/80, HR 86, RR 14, Temp 98.5 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 174 lb, stable.
General: alert, cooperative, mildly anxious appearing.
HEENT: pupils equal and reactive.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Skin: no track marks or lesions.
Psych: linear thought process, fair insight, future-oriented and engaged.
Labs (drawn in the ED): comprehensive metabolic panel within normal limits, urine drug screen reviewed with patient.

A/P:
1. Psychoactive substance dependence, active, engaged in outpatient treatment. Continue group and individual counseling and current medication-assisted treatment. Reviewed a relapse-prevention plan and evening coping strategies. Provided program crisis line information and confirmed next appointment.
2. Supportive care: discussed sleep hygiene and stress management around work hours. Coordinated with the case manager on scheduling so he can attend all sessions.
3. Function and work: symptoms are affecting his ability to keep regular shifts. Discussed documentation to support a gradual return to a steady schedule.

Return to the program in 1 week, sooner if cravings escalate or he feels unsafe.
